look_here_first: Inspect the END of one intact comb and look for a conspicuous bare, pointed branch-axis extension ('stinger') beyond the last spikelets. On fresh branches check for long spreading hairs and on basal blades for papillose-based hairs. Hairiness alone varies and does not trump terminal spikelet/rachis anatomy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents native/herbarium records from Burnet, Comal, and Hays counties, among additional project-zone counties.

best_field_traits: papillose-based hairs especially near blade margins/base
branch axis extends beyond terminal spikelets as a naked point

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Bouteloua pectinata, B. hirsuta is generally shorter and less robust, with fewer/shorter inflorescence branches and a longer flowering window. Compared with B. trifida, it has broader comb-like branches with many more tightly packed spikelets.
crew_field_steps: Find an intact one-sided flowering comb; don't just notice its purple or tan color.
Trace the branch to its naked projecting tip beyond the packed spikelets. The inspected close photo shows that needlelike extension clearly.
Examine the long spreading hairs on branch and basal blade margins; compare blue grama, which usually lacks the long bare terminal rachis.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole flowering plant with number of racemes on same culm and height context.
True branch-tip extreme macro showing spikelets stop BEFORE extended naked rachis.
Papillose-based basal leaf/blade hair macro and sheath/ligule.
Mature comb and spikelets against a millimeter ruler next to B. gracilis/B. pectinata.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with blue grama, hairy grama has more conspicuously hairy reproductive parts and a naked projecting rachis tip; blue comb spikelets continue toward the tip. Taller B. pectinata often has longer, straighter and more numerous combs, but their features overlap enough to require mature units and provenance. Texas grama bears several very short highly awned/fuzzy branches rather than a few longer solid combs.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Grama field check — Hairy grama
steps: FIRST PHOTO: inspect the taxon-labelled Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata flowering-branch image with the existing two gross pointers to conspicuous hairs and its projecting naked rachis tip; it is NOT whole-plant habit despite its old filename.

SECOND PHOTO: use Matt Lavin's side-view of the same-species flowering comb to trace the spikelet-bearing region into the narrow, naked distal extension; distinguish projecting rachis tissue from fine awns.
THIRD PHOTO: compare Patrick Alexander's flowering branch with hanging pale anthers; pollen structures here do not establish glume, lemma or ligule anatomy.

COMPARE the actual blue grama look-alike panel: spikelets generally continue closer to the comb tip; do not certify the species from purple color or hairiness without matched mature flowering branches.

LAST-MILE PHOTOS: one genuinely rooted, entire hairy grama plant showing its culms and basal blade margins; a split inner collar with true ligule and 1-mm scale; an intact mature spikelet and separated glumes, fertile/sterile lemmas and awns from one source-determined individual.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Hairy grama: inspect the end of one intact comb for a bare rachis tip extending 5–10 mm past the final spikelets; check papillose-based hairs on glume midveins and basal blade margins. Do not diagnose solely by purple color or the word 'hairy'.

measurable_diagnostics.growth_form: Warm-season tufted perennial, sometimes short-stoloniferous; culms approximately 15–75 cm in Iowa State's grass treatment, commonly 20–50 cm in Texas field descriptions.
measurable_diagnostics.ligule_collar: Ligule a fringe of hairs approximately 0.2–0.5 mm (Iowa State); collar may be hairy, auricles not used as a species character. Photograph the actual blade/sheath junction and papillose-based marginal hairs with mm scale.
measurable_diagnostics.flowering_architecture: Usually 1–4 short one-sided combs; each often 1.5–3 cm long with approximately 20–50 closely packed spikelets. Bare terminal rachis projects about 5–10 mm beyond the final spikelets; measure from last spikelet, not from comb base.
measurable_diagnostics.spikelet_glumes: Spikelets approximately 5–6 mm; each with one fertile and one or two reduced sterile florets. Lower glume approximately 1.4–3.5 mm, upper approximately 3–6 mm, with papillose-based hairs particularly on upper-glume midvein.
measurable_diagnostics.lemmas_florets_awns: Fertile lemma approximately 2–4.5 mm, often pubescent and 1–3 short-awned (central awn approximately 0.2–2.5 mm). Reduced sterile lemma often bilobed and 3-awned, awns approximately 2–4(–6) mm. The naked rachis 'stinger' is NOT a lemma awn.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Bouteloua gracilis (blue grama) usually has more spikelets per comb and little bare rachis extension beyond the last spikelet, and is less papillose-hairy; B. pectinata can have more numerous/longer combs but overlaps and may hybridize, requiring a complete specimen and current taxonomy; B. trifida has very short, more feathery branches rather than the solid comb of hairy grama.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Whole rooted perennial crown and complete flowering culm with comb count, plus matched blue grama at same scale.
Undamaged comb tip with a 1-mm ruler proving 5–10 mm bare terminal rachis; annotate the rachis, not a floret awn.
Upper glume papillose-based hairs at 10–20× with 1-mm bar and separately basal blade-margin hairs and true ligule.
One dissected 5–6 mm spikelet with lower/upper glumes, fertile lemma and reduced sterile lemma separately exposed; show which awns attach to which lemma.
Matched B. gracilis/B. pectinata flowering branches with individually verified image rights and identification.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS. Require measured spikelet/lemma/ligule and true rachis-tip photo verification, public image permissions, and arrow/site QA before FINISHED; preserve existing photo attribution and nativity/taxonomy holds.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_scope: Morphology from published treatments, not newly measured from existing gallery pixels. No taxonomic or range change.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — NAKED COMB-TIP STINGER
field_id_short_tiles.short: On one intact hairy grama comb, trace the bare rachis about 5–10 mm beyond the last spikelet.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Existing species panels 1–3 show spreading hairs and the exposed terminal branch-axis extension. That pointed RACHIS is not an awn attached to a lemma. Measure the bare part from the final attached spikelet on a mature undamaged comb; existing photos establish the silhouette, not a calibrated 5–10 mm measurement.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL PIXEL-VISIBLE BRANCH TIP — MEASURED TIP STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL TUFT, TRUE LIGULE AND COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Tufted perennial; at the blade–sheath seam seek a very short 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published Iowa State treatment describes a hair-fringe ligule about 0.2–0.5 mm. Separate true inner-junction ligule hairs from the longer papillose-based hairs on basal blade margins and from branch hairs. The three archived target photographs do not demonstrate a complete rooted crown or calibrated true ligule. Do not add an anatomy arrow without a real exposed collar.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT COMBS AND MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 1–4 one-sided combs, each about 1.5–3 cm with roughly 20–50 spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published ranges, not measurements from the unscaled images. Count branches on ONE connected flowering culm, then use a millimeter ruler on a mature comb and an intact ~5–6 mm spikelet. The naked 5–10 mm rachis tip and the spikelet body are separate measurements.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL TARGET COMBS — SCALE AND COMPLETE CULM MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, TWO FLORETS AND AWN ORIGINS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet ~5–6 mm; lower glume ~1.4–3.5 mm, upper ~3–6 mm; fertile lemma ~2–4.5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: A mature spikelet has a fertile basal floret and one or two reduced sterile florets. Dissect BOTH glumes separately. The fertile lemma may have short awns (central ~0.2–2.5 mm), while the reduced sterile lemma often has THREE awns about 2–4(–6) mm. Do not mistake the terminal naked rachis for a lemma awn or infer which floret carries a bristle from an overview image.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED REPRODUCTIVE ANATOMY — DISSECTED 1-MM-SCALE PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Blue grama usually lacks the long bare stinger; pectinata often has longer, more numerous combs.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Comparison panel 4 is BLUE GRAMA, not hairy grama. Bouteloua gracilis usually has 1–3 curved eyebrow combs with spikelets reaching close to their tips; hairy grama has spreading reproductive hairs and a conspicuous bare tip. B. pectinata may overlap in size and hairiness, and B. trifida has much shorter narrow appressed branches. Compare ripe spikelets and verified rachis tips, not purple color alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL LOOK-ALIKE PANEL — SAME-SCALE COMPARISON NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: three real archived species photos, but decisive measured microanatomy is missing.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): one voucher-linked rooted Central Texas perennial with entire flowering culm and comb count; 1-mm-calibrated 5–10 mm naked rachis tip; true 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule plus basal papillose hairs; intact ~5–6 mm spikelet with separately exposed glumes, fertile and sterile lemmas and distinct awn origins; matched blue grama and pectinata combs. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify all three physical JPEGs, individual CC BY-SA 4.0 / CC BY-SA 2.0 / CC0 1.0 credits and conditions, six existing gross arrows against actual pixels, other-species panel labels, six tile layouts and live/mobile display. Do not mark FINISHED or claim a new photograph/arrow.

Published ranges, not image-derived measurements.
